messages:
Anna: Heads-up — the A/B experiment (rollout id r-92f3) we put at 20/80 split is triggering quota throttles in eu-west and we’re seeing spikes in user-side latencies. dashboard shows rise in latency_p50 and kv_miss_rate since 11:32. @srebot posted alerts. :rotating_light:

SREBot: ALERT: rollout:r-92f3 error_rate > 3% for 6m, region=eu-west, affected_routes=chat.generate. See /alerts/1845123448

Mike: ok grabbing context. is traffic split still 20% canary?

Anna: yes 20% canary -> variant B (quantized-opt). Baseline A is 80%. SDK telemetry shows degraded tail latency for B.

Jess: oncall here. Suggest we do fast revert to A=100% while we triage. But note: B has a different KV cache prefix and if we flip traffic hard we risk having mix of cached prefixes causing duplicate state and inference cache churn. Need to invalidate prefix for B after flip.

Vikram: agree. Also B uses session-affinity header X-Session-ID -> some requests are sticky to nodes with warmed KV entries. Fast 100% flip is fine but we must: 1) set routing guard to reject new sessions to B, 2) flip split to 100/0, 3) drain B pods, 4) invalidate B cache prefix.

Mike: propose runbook (fast-path):
```
# 1. Set rollout guard to pause new canary allocations
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://internal.redwood/api/rollouts/r-92f3/guard -d '{"pause_new":true}'
# 2. Flip traffic: A:100 B:0
PATCH https://internal.redwood/api/rollouts/r-92f3 -d '{"traffic":{"A":100,"B":0}}'
# 3. Drain B pool:
rbctl drain --pool rollout-r-92f3-canary --timeout 120
# 4. Invalidate prefix used by B:
redis-cli -h kv-prod --eval 'delprefix' "rb:rollouts:r-92f3:B:"
```

Jess: add one more safety — set quota-limiter to enforce soft 5% cutoff so we don't flip back and forth due to a short blip. And run async job to recompute KV TTLs after invalidation.

Anna: can we do this via Console (quick) or do we need the curl commands? I can click through Console for traffic flip.

Mike: Console has a one-click revert but it doesn't run the cache invalidation. I'll run the API flip and then kick off a cache invalidation job.

Vikram: Also verify monitoring hooks: ensure trace sampling includes the new baseline traces and the rollout-trace tag. If latency doesn't drop after flip + invalidate, we escalate to runtime.

Jess: executing now: setting guard -> :white_check_mark:

SREBot: ACTION: guard set by Jess at 11:37 (r-92f3).

Mike: flipping traffic to A=100 now.

SREBot: ACTION: traffic updated by Mike at 11:38 (A=100,B=0).

Mike: draining canary pool (rbctl output: 12 connections gracefully terminated, 0 forced)

Jess: kicking cache invalidation job:
```
POST https://internal.redwood/jobs -d '{"type":"invalidate-kv-prefix","prefix":"rb:rollouts:r-92f3:B:"}'
```

Anna: telemetry looks better already — latency_p50 down, error_rate trending to normal. Great.

Vikram: leaving canary pool drained and cache invalidated. Keep guard on for 15m.

Jess: will keep an eye and reopen if regressions. Good job. :thumbsup:

Anna: filing follow-up ticket to root cause the quantized-opt infra mismatch (will assign to runtime + ml infra)
